JUDGEMENT CALLS
  * S15 (375,607) -> JUNCTION. The 10mF capacitor's bottom lead is one unbroken stroke that runs down through the bottom rail and ends on the GND bar at y~640, so the crop shows a plain 4-way X (deg=5 in the tracer's count because the GND bar's two ends are branches too). No solder dot, no hop, no jog - verified at 8x. Junction, for the same three reasons as the equivalent site on circuit_351: the ink prior says a plain crossing is a junction; drafter habit gives no counter-evidence because this sheet has no solder dots anywhere (every other node, S3 included, is a bare T); and the crossing reading is physically perverse - it would make net 0 just {Capacitor #4 bottom, GND} and leave {Resistor #3 bottom, V-DC minus terminal} as a separate ungrounded rail, i.e. a drafter deliberately routing a wire across a rail to reach a ground symbol rather than simply grounding the rail. The tracer's hop=3.6 score here is spurious; the pixels show a straight vertical through the rail with no arc.
  * S3 (381,465) -> JUNCTION, recorded explicitly. Unambiguous deg-3 T at 8x: the east branch to the inductor starts on the through-running centre column. The alternative is not even expressible here (a T has no opposite pair to pass through).
